test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: One-quarter of a circular pizza of radius 21 cm was removed from the whole pizza. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the remaining pizza? (Use π = (22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When 1/4 of a circular pizza is removed, the remaining shape consists of 3/4 of the original circumference plus two straight edges equal to the radius.

Perimeter = (3/4) × 2πr + 2r

Perimeter = (3/4) × 2 × (22/7) × 21 + (2 × 21)

Perimeter = 99 + 42 = 141 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 141 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b438551a0cf2fa7575c9c2e320edae4bef12707c96d94c48df3c58a1dee4f756.png] 

**Given:**

Radius of the circular pizza (r) = 21 cm

Part removed = 1/4 of the pizza

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of remaining shape = Length of remaining arc + 2 × Radius

Length of arc = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Angle of the remaining pizza (θ) = 360° − (1/4 × 360°) = 270°

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (270° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 21

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (3/4) × 2 × 22 × 3

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (3/4) × 132 = 99 cm

⇒ Total straight edges = 2 × Radius = 2 × 21 = 42 cm

⇒ Perimeter of remaining pizza = 99 + 42 = 141 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 141 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Semicircle

A semicircle's perimeter includes half the circumference and the full straight diameter: P = πr + 2r = r(π + 2).

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc is proportional to its central angle θ: Arc Length = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ is a fraction of the total area: Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².
